questions.question: When turning on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Keep your eyes focused close to the front of the motorcycle.
Look ahead to where you want to go.
Turn your entire body to see through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead to where you want to go.
questions.explanation: When turning, look ahead to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: A major effect of drinking alcohol is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down body functions.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows down your body and mind.

questions.question: To reduce crash risk, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Be ready to react to hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hope another driver sees you.
questions.explanation: To stay safe, make yourself visible to others. Signal your plans with proper turns and lane position. Keep space around you and watch for hazards ahead.

questions.question: A face shield should:

options.text: Provide a clear view to both sides.
Block all air from passing through it.
Fit so tight that glasses cannot fit under it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provide a clear view to both sides.
questions.explanation: A good face shield must be scratch-free, tough, and let you see clearly to both sides. It should fasten securely, allow air to pass through, and have room for glasses if needed.

questions.question: Group riders should avoid riding in pairs because:

options.text: A merging driver may not see both riders.
Helmet reflections may make it hard to see.
Riders do not have enough space to move around hazards.
Riders on the left cannot exit the highway easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders do not have enough space to move around hazards.
questions.explanation: Riding in pairs is not safe. Neither rider will have enough room to move and avoid hazards.

questions.question: A person is legally intoxicated with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ______ or higher.
questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent
questions.explanation: For people age 21 and older, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher means they are legally intoxicated. It is illegal and dangerous to ride while intoxicated.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you, you should:

options.text: Ignore them and focus on the road ahead.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Ride on the shoulder to let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes to let a tailgater pass. Do not speed up—that just increases danger. Never ride on the shoulder because drivers do not expect you to be there.

questions.question: A motorcyclist is well-protected when wearing:

options.text: Shoes that stop below the ankle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather gloves.
questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs. Wear tall, sturdy boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles. Choose footwear with low heels. Leather gloves protect your hands in a crash and give you a better grip on the controls.

questions.question: When a vehicle passes you on your left, you should:

options.text: Move as far right as possible to help them.
Move to the shoulder to help them.
Ride in the center of your lane.
Ride on the left side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Stay in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side nearest the passing vehicle risks a collision. Riding on the far side tempts them to merge back too soon. The center is the safest position.

questions.question: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles helps because:

options.text: You can pass danger more quickly.
You have a narrower view to stay focused.
You have more time to react to what others do.
You can follow the next vehicle more easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have more time to react to what others do.
questions.explanation: Space between you and other vehicles gives you a clearer view of hazards, more time to react, and more room to move around them.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: After at least an hour of riding.
After more than 8 hours of riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips less than five miles long, usually a few minutes after the rider starts.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, you should:

options.text: Grip the handlebars firmly and gradually close the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and gradually close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up because it will make the wobble worse. Instead, hold the handlebars tight and slow down by gradually closing the throttle. Move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you can. Avoid using the brakes, as this may also make the wobble worse.

questions.question: If you are being chased by a dog, you should:

options.text: Stop until the animal loses interest.
Approach the animal slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the animal slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: If a dog chases your motorcycle, downshift and move toward it slowly. Once you are close, accelerate and leave it behind. Do not try to kick it.

questions.question: Use your mirrors when stopped at an intersection:

options.text: To see if vehicles parked on the sides of the street are entering traffic.
To look for vehicles changing lanes.
To watch for vehicles behind you that may not be slowing down.
To see if someone is planning to turn behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: To watch for vehicles behind you that may not be slowing down.
questions.explanation: When stopped at an intersection, use your mirrors to check for cars coming from behind. Drivers may not see you until they are close, so you need to be ready to react.

questions.question: Riders who do not wear helmets are ________ to die in a crash than riders who do wear helmets.
questions.correctAnswerText: Three times as likely
questions.explanation: At any speed, riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders wearing helmets.

questions.question: Where is the clutch lever usually located?
questions.correctAnswerText: On the left handgrip
questions.explanation: The clutch lever is usually on the left handgrip of a motorcycle.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger or cargo:

options.text: It may take less time to accelerate, but more time to stop.
It may take more time to accelerate and stop.
It may take more time to accelerate, but less time to stop.
It may take less time to accelerate and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may take more time to accelerate and stop.
questions.explanation: Extra weight from cargo or a passenger makes your motorcycle take longer to speed up and slower to stop than when you ride alone.

questions.question: A motorcyclist's cushion of space:

options.text: Should vary according to riding conditions.
Is not necessary in most situations.
Should be avoided to keep traffic moving safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should vary according to riding conditions.
questions.explanation: You need more space between you and other vehicles if your motorcycle takes longer to stop. Increase your distance on slippery pavement, when you cannot see ahead, or when traffic is heavy and a driver might cut in front of you.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: A skidding rear tire:

options.text: Eliminates your ability to change direction.
Is only a concern if the front tire is also skidding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Eliminates your ability to change direction.
questions.explanation: A skidding rear tire is dangerous and can cause a violent crash. Too much rear brake pressure locks the rear wheel. When the wheel locks, you cannot change direction. You must release the brake to regain control.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves when riding in a group?

options.text: In the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This way, they won't fall behind, and experienced riders can watch them from behind.

questions.question: What should you do if you must ride over an obstacle?

options.text: Slow down as much as possible.
Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Stay on your seat and lift your feet from the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as much as possible.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle, slow down and hit it at a 90-degree angle if possible. Keep your motorcycle straight up. Just before impact, ease off the throttle to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: What should you do if a dog is chasing you?

options.text: Stop and wait until it loses interest.
Move slowly toward it, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move slowly toward it, then speed up.
questions.explanation: Dogs often chase motorcycles. If chased by a dog, slow down and approach it. Then speed up and leave it behind.

questions.question: Which item gives a rider the best protection?
questions.correctAnswerText: A face shield
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles protect your eyes only. A windshield or eyeglasses do not provide adequate protection.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When you can see through the vehicle in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the roadway is wet.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when your motorcycle needs a longer distance to stop. Also increase it in heavy traffic or when you cannot see through the vehicle ahead.
